analyst_view.overall: Early view: Albacete have won three in a row under Joseba Etxeberria, the latest 3-1 at Leganés, where a Leganés goal was disallowed after VAR spotted Morata's elbow on Jesús Vallejo, but they are still 21st. Celta Fortuna, Celta's reserve side, are 16th after a 2-1 defeat at Burgos and arrive with a long absence list, including three suspensions (Adrià Capdevila, Enrique Ribes, Hugo López). I found little fresh team news this week; lineups and the referee will be added closer to the Monday-night kick-off.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals, which fits the context: Celta Fortuna's league games average more than three goals (19-25 in 13) and they will field a patched-up side again. Against that, Albacete have scored only 13 in 13 and are without José Corpas, so I hold at the site's figure.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.1 corners, with 6.3 for Albacete. I lean lower: Etxeberria's Albacete have been winning by scoring and defending, not by dominating, and Celta Fortuna pass more (5,515 passes to Albacete's 4,739 by LaLiga's count), so they should have more of the ball than the split suggests.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.5 cards. I lean higher: Albacete press high under Etxeberria, Corpas was sent off recently, and Celta Fortuna have 37 yellows and three players already banned for accumulation. A Monday-night game between 21st and 16th should be scrappy.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.2 shots. I lean lower, mainly on Albacete's side: LaLiga counts them at 113 shots in 13 games, under nine a game, so 16.2 at home does not match how they play. Celta Fortuna (119 in 13) can contribute their share.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.4 shots on target. I lean lower with the shots: Albacete's wins have come from few attempts, and Celta Fortuna rely heavily on Álvaro Marín (eight goals) with Óscar Marcos, their joint second scorer, reported injured by one source.
